entries.title: Jeremiah 51:1
segments: Babylon was one of the mightiest empires which the world ever saw, and it made itself conspicuous above all other nations of ancient times by persecuting God's covenant people.  For this reason it stands in the Scriptures as the representative of all organized forms of persecution, whether secular or spiritual.  Its terrible overthrow, so complete and so perpetual, is both a proof of God's power, and a pledge of his purpose to destroy and break in pieces every thing that exalts itself against the kingdom of his Son, however great may be its power and resources.  All who join themselves to his enemies shall perish; but "blessed are all they that put their trust in him."

entries.title: Jeremiah 51:5
segments: Though their land was filled with sin; more literally, "for their land," the land of the Babylonians, "is filled."

entries.title: Jeremiah 51:7
segments:
Babylon--a golden cup; the wine-cup of God's wrath.  She is called a golden cup to indicate her great wealth. 
 
  Have drunken of her wine; have suffered divine inflictions through her agency.  In
, the figure is used in a different way, to express the intoxication of error and sin.

entries.title: Jeremiah 51:9
segments: We would have healed Babylon; the allies of Babylon speak.

entries.title: Jeremiah 51:12
segments: Upon the walls of Babylon; or, "against the walls of Babylon."

entries.title: Jeremiah 51:13
segments: The measure of thy covetousness; it is full for punishment. Compare

entries.title: Jeremiah 51:14
segments: With men; that is, troops of enemies.

entries.title: Jeremiah 51:15
segments:

entries.title: Jeremiah 51:20
segments: Thou art my battle-axe; that is, Babylon, as the instrument which God has employed to punish the nations,

; but some understand these words of Cyrus. 
 
  Will I break in pieces; or, "I have broken in pieces."

entries.title: Jeremiah 51:25
segments: O destroying mountain; Babylon is here compared to a volcanic mountain, which has sent forth desolating streams of fire over all the nations.  But she shall be thrust down from her high position, and made a mass of burnt and broken fragments.

entries.title: Jeremiah 51:27
segments: Ararat, Minni, and Ashchenaz; provinces of Armenia, or of adjacent regions.

entries.title: Jeremiah 51:31
segments: At one end; literally, "at the end."  The armies of Cyrus marched into Babylon at both ends, through he channel of the Euphrates, the waters of which they had turned off while the Babylonians were engaged in feasting.

entries.title: Jeremiah 51:32
segments:
The passages; probably those which connected the two parts of the city. 
 
  The reeds; literally, "the marshes;" probably marshes covered with tall reeds, that impeded the march of the enemy.

entries.title: Jeremiah 51:34
segments: Cast me out; from my own land.  Zion is the speaker.

entries.title: Jeremiah 51:36
segments: Dry up her sea; this seems to be a prophetic allusion to the way in which the city was taken, by the drawing off of the waters of the Euphrates, so as to afford a passage to the army of Cyrus through its channel.

entries.title: Jeremiah 51:39
segments: In their heat; whole they are inflamed with wine.  See note on

. 
 
  I will make their feasts; Jehovah will himself prepare for them another banquet, even a deadly cup; that is, destruction by the armies of Cyrus. 
 
  Rejoice; rave, after the manner of the drunken.

entries.title: Jeremiah 51:41
segments: Sheshach; see note on

entries.title: Jeremiah 51:42
segments: The sea; the desolating armies of the Medes. Compare

entries.title: Jeremiah 51:46
segments: And lest your heart faint, and ye fear; better, "And let not your heart faint, that ye should fear."  In such a time of confusion many discouraging rumors would reach the ears of the returning exiles; these they are exhorted to disregard.

entries.title: Jeremiah 51:51
segments: We are confounded; the prophet here speaks in the name of God's covenant people.

entries.title: Jeremiah 51:55
segments: The great voice; the tumult of her vast population, which is compared to the roaring of the waves of the sea.

entries.title: Jeremiah 51:58
segments:
The broad walls--high gates; according to Herodotus, the walls of Babylon were four-square, three hundred and fifty feet high, and eighty-seven thick, with twenty-five gates of solid brass on each side. 
 
  In the fire; or, "for the fire."  They shall gather wealth only to be consumed by fire.

entries.title: Jeremiah 51:61
segments: Read all the words; to the captive Jews residing there.

entries.title: Jeremiah 51:64
segments: They shall be weary; the Babylonians shall sink down exhausted and powerless.
Thus far are the words of Jeremiah; the following chapter seems to have been added to the book by some inspired writer, perhaps Ezra.
